managedData.heading: Edstellar L&D outsourcing, from strategy to delivery.
managedData.description: Edstellar can run your whole learning function, from strategy and content to delivery, technology and vendors. Here is the honest trade-off between covering that span in-house and handing it to a managed service.

inHouseCard.title: Keeping L&D in-house
items: One small team stretched across strategy, content, delivery, technology and vendors.
Fixed headcount sits idle in quiet months and is overwhelmed in busy ones.
Quality and cost swing by which vendor and region delivered.
Reporting is manual, so impact is hard to prove.

managedCard.title: Running it as a managed service
items: One partner runs the whole span, from strategy to delivery, or just the parts you choose.
Cost flexes with demand and stays predictable per learner.
One standard of delivery across every region and language.
Impact reported every quarter against agreed SLAs.

items.question: How is a training needs analysis different from just running a survey?
items.answer: A survey tells you what people say they want. A needs analysis triangulates that against performance data, role requirements and business goals, then separates real skill gaps from problems training cannot fix. The output is a ranked plan, not a wish list.

items.question: How long does an engagement take?
items.answer: A focused analysis typically runs four to eight weeks, depending on the number of roles and functions in scope. Enterprise-wide diagnostics tied to a transformation can run longer. You get a clear timeline in the proposal.

items.question: What do we actually receive at the end?
items.answer: A skill-gap heatmap, a competency map, a risk-ranked roadmap, a finance-ready business case, and a measurement baseline. Working artifacts your team can act on and reuse, not a one-off presentation.

items.question: Can you analyze needs without selling us the training afterward?
items.answer: Yes. The analysis is a standalone service. If a gap is best closed another way, or not by training at all, that is what the roadmap will say. Edstellar can deliver the programs if you want, but the diagnosis stands on its own.

items.question: How do you prove the training worked once it runs?
items.answer: Measurement is designed in at the start. We set the baseline and the metrics before delivery, so impact is compared against a known starting point rather than argued about later.

items.question: We already have a competency framework. Does that change things?
items.answer: It helps. We work with your existing framework where one exists, calibrate it against role requirements, and only rebuild what is missing or out of date, so you are not paying to reinvent what already works.

items.question: Is a training needs analysis the same as a learning needs analysis?
items.answer: Yes. Training needs analysis (TNA or TNI) and learning needs analysis (LNA or LNI) are interchangeable terms for the same work: measuring the gap between the capability a role requires and the capability your people have today, then turning it into a prioritized plan. Whichever term your organization uses, this is the engagement it describes.
